title: [v0.4.29] macOS: run Quadlet inside Podman Machine
author: patplu
body:
Parent: #818 · Release: v0.4.29 #876 · Consumed by: #822

## Decision (2026-10-14)

Podman Machine on macOS reuses the **existing Podman Quadlet realization**, executed **inside the Podman Machine Linux VM**. There will be no second Podman realization: no Docker-compat-API shortcut and no `podman kube play`/compose variant.

```text
macOS host
  └── native baha (renders the same Quadlet units as on Linux)
        └── executor: podman machine (ssh) ──> Fedora CoreOS VM
              ├── ~/.config/containers/systemd/*.container
              ├── systemctl --user / journalctl --user
              └── rootless Podman workloads
```

This follows the boundary already set in #818/#820/#822: Quadlet/systemd stays a **Podman Linux realization** and is never claimed to run natively on Darwin.

## Problem

The Podman provider calls host commands and the host filesystem directly. There are roughly 40 `exec`/`os.*` call sites across ~13 files, mainly `quadlet_runtime.go` (19), `quadlet_project.go`, `quadlet_images.go`, `lifecycle.go`, `quadlet_resources.go` and `quadlet_systemctl.go`, and `quadletUserUnitDir()` resolves a local path. On macOS `QuadletAvailable` is false, so `podman.New` returns `ErrRuntimeNotFound` (`internal/providers/runtime/podman/provider.go:51`). An installed Podman is therefore reported as *not found*, which is a dead-end diagnostic.

## Required work

1. Add a narrow **executor seam inside the Podman provider**: run a command, read/write/remove a unit file, resolve the unit directory and the runtime environment (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`). It has two implementations:
   - `local`: today's behavior on Linux, byte-for-byte equivalent.
   - `machine`: the selected Podman Machine, reached through `podman machine ssh <name>` or the machine's ssh identity and port from `podman machine inspect`.

   The seam is provider-internal. It is not part of the Host Platform Contract and not a generic remote-exec facility, and it is not exposed via MCP. Bind execution to the explicitly selected machine/endpoint and its verified owner; verify the selected SSH identity/host boundary, unit-directory ownership and path mappings. No fallback to another machine, host daemon or unchecked generic SSH destination.
2. **Machine discovery and selection:** default machine or the Target's explicit machine name; running/stopped state; observed rootless/rootful privilege plus positively verified VM execution/isolation (D1 in #876/#819); never infer trustworthy isolation from rootful status alone; systemd/Quadlet generator availability inside the VM.
3. **Path mapping:** bind-mount sources must be visible in the VM. Podman Machine mounts `$HOME` (`/Users/...`) via virtiofs at the same path by default. Paths outside the configured machine volumes fail before mutation with a typed diagnostic that names the path and the `podman machine` volume remedy.
4. **Ownership/evidence parity:** labels, unit names, owned-resource removal, retirement, logs and explorer units behave exactly as on Linux; ownership checks never trust the macOS host for VM-side state.
5. **Typed diagnostics instead of `ErrRuntimeNotFound`:** report Podman not installed, no machine, machine stopped, Quadlet unavailable in the VM and path not shared as distinct causes, each with a concrete next action.

## Testing

- Unit: fake executor conformance, with identical rendered units and command sequences for `local` and `machine`.
- Linux: existing rootless Podman/Quadlet acceptance stays green (no regression).
- macOS: real Podman Machine Dev Local journey on the self-hosted Mac runner (see the runner issue linked in #823): init/plan/up/status/doctor/logs/sql/cache/owned destroy, plus negative cases (stopped machine, unshared path, missing machine).

## Non-goals

- No Quadlet/systemd concept in the Host Platform Contract.
- No support for Podman Desktop-specific APIs; plain `podman machine` only.
- No Windows/WSL2 Podman Machine work here (#821 owns WSL2).

## Acceptance

- [ ] One Podman realization; the `machine` executor produces the same units and ownership as `local`.
- [ ] Linux Podman acceptance unchanged.
- [ ] Real macOS Podman Machine Dev Local journey passes on an exact SHA.
- [ ] Every Podman Machine failure mode is typed and actionable; no `ErrRuntimeNotFound` for an installed Podman.

- [ ] Endpoint/machine mismatch, unknown VM provenance, changed SSH/owner boundary and unauthorized host path/socket sharing are rejected with typed diagnostics under D1 in #876.
